title: A blunt knife
translation: A good craftsman, they say, works with a knife that's a little blunt. The sculptor Myōkan's knife never cut very well.
original: よき{細工|さいく}は、{少|すこ}し{鈍|にぶ}き{刀|かたな}をつかふといふ。
{妙観|めうくわん}が{刀|かたな}はいたく{立|た}たず。
literal: A good craftsman, it is said, uses a slightly dull blade.
Myōkan's blade did not bite much.

notes.text: {細工|さいく}: here a craftsman, someone who makes fine things by hand. Modern {細工|さいく} is the work itself, 'craftwork'.
{刀|かたな}: any single-edged blade, here a carving knife, not a sword.
The 1925 edition identifies Myōkan as a priest of Katsuoji in Settsu province, who carved the temple's statue of Kannon.
{立|た}つ: of a blade, 'to cut in, to bite'. いたく … ず: 'not very'. The text gives no reason why a blunt knife is better. It states the saying and gives one example.
